findings.title: Breaking API removal: findMany deleted without updating callers
findings.body: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts removes the public method findMany (which executed bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with combined where) and replaces it with getBaseConditions returning Prisma.Sql. If any existing caller still calls service.findMany, TypeScript compilation fails or runtime throws TypeError. The diff shows no caller migration in this PR, so this is a breaking change that must be coordinated with all consumers or keep findMany as a wrapper around the new raw query.

findings.title: Public options type weakens team-scope validation
findings.body: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts introduces InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with optional teamId for all scopes, replacing the discriminated-union InsightsBookingServiceOptions constructor param. This allows scope:'team' without teamId to type-check, only to fail Zod safeParse at runtime and silently return NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0). The previous type required teamId for team scope at compile time. Preserve the discriminated union for the public type to catch invalid calls statically.

findings.title: Order-dependent ANY array assertion makes org-scope test flaky
findings.body: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts expects getAuthorizationConditions to equal Prisma.sql with teamIds [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds [user.id, user2.id, user3.id] using toEqual. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds database order, which is not guaranteed, and dedupes via Set preserving fetch order. Any different row order produces a different values array and fails the test even though SQL semantics are identical. Sort IDs or compare strings/values order-insensitively.
